heroData.title: Hire in Canada Without a Subsidiary
heroData.subtitle: Compliant Employer of Record services
heroData.description: Deploy teams across all provinces/territories (including Quebec) in days. The EOR handles CPP, EI, and provincial health taxes.
heroData.bestFor: Testing the market, cross-border remote teams.

steps.title: Service Agreement
steps.description: Sign MSA with the EOR provider. Define salary, role, and benefits packages.

steps.title: Employee Invitation
steps.description: EOR sends invite to candidate to upload TD1 (tax forms), void cheque, and ID.

steps.title: Contract Issuance
steps.description: EOR issues a compliant employment contract. MUST be in French for Quebec employees (Bill 96).

steps.title: Benefits Enrollment
steps.description: Employee selects health/dental coverage. Coverage typically starts on Day 1.

steps.title: SIN Validation
steps.description: EOR validates Social Insurance Number with Service Canada to ensure work eligibility.

items.title: Quebec Bill 96
items.text: Strict French language laws apply. All employment documents, communications, and software must be available in French. Non-compliance risks significant fines.

items.title: Permanent Establishment
items.text: Using an EOR for >18-24 months or for revenue-generating roles (Sales Directors) significantly increases PE risk. Transition to a local entity is recommended for long-term presence.

items.title: Termination Laws
items.text: Canadian common law often requires 'reasonable notice' far exceeding statutory minimums (approx. 1 month per year of service). EORs usually indemnify themselves against this cost.

items.title: Benefits Expectations
items.text: While healthcare is public, top talent expects supplemental private health/dental insurance (Extended Health Benefits).

items.title: Vacation Norms
items.text: 2 weeks is statutory minimum (3 after 5 years), but professional roles typically expect 3-4 weeks.

faqs.question: Can I hire independent contractors through an EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, known as 'Agent of Record' services. However, Canada confirms worker classification strictly (T4 vs T4A). Misclassification penalties are severe.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle stock options?
faqs.answer: EORs usually cannot grant stock options directly (NSOs/ISOs) as they are the legal employer. They can facilitate 'shadow equity' or cash-equivalent bonus plans.

faqs.question: Is a deposit required?
faqs.answer: Yes, almost all Canadian EORs require a refundable deposit equivalent to 1-2 months of total payroll cost to cover cash flow.

steps.title: Gross Pay Calculation
steps.description: Calculate base salary + commissions + bonuses. Verify provincial minimum wage compliance.

steps.title: Deductions (Source)
steps.description: Deduct Employee CPP (5.95%), EI (1.64%), and Federal/Provincial Income Tax.

steps.title: Net Pay Distribution
steps.description: Direct deposit (EFT) to employees. Pay stub generation (mandatory).

steps.title: CRA Remittance
steps.description: Remit employer + employee portions to CRA by the 15th of the following month (for regular remitters).

steps.title: EHT/WCB Filing
steps.description: File provincial health taxes (e.g. BC EHT, QC HSF) and workers comp premiums separately.

items.title: T4 Filing Deadline
items.text: Must file T4 slips by February 28th (March 7th for 2025). Late filing penalties start at $100 per slip.

items.title: Vacation Accrual
items.text: Vacation pay (4% or 6%) must be accrued as a liability or paid out on every cheque. 'Use it or lose it' policies are illegal in many provinces.

items.title: CPP2 Bracket 2025
items.text: New separate CPP2 contribution applies on earnings between $71,300 and $81,200.

faqs.question: What is the frequency of payroll in Canada?
faqs.answer: Bi-weekly (every 2 weeks) and Semi-monthly (15th and last day) are most common. Monthly payroll is permitted in some provinces but less common for employees.

faqs.question: Do I need a CAD bank account?
faqs.answer: Yes, to remit directly to the CRA, a Canadian business bank account is typically required. Non-resident importers may use a third-party processor.

items.title: CPP (Pension Plan)
items.text: 2025 Employee Contribution: 5.95% up to YMPE ($71,300), plus 4% on YAMPE ($81,100). Employer matches 100%.

items.title: EI (Employment Insurance)
items.text: 2025 Employee Rate: 1.63% (1.27% in Quebec) up to Max Insurable Earnings ($65,700). Employer pays 1.4x of employee amount.

items.title: Vacation Pay
items.text: Minimum 4% of gross wages (2 weeks). Must be paid out on every cheque OR accrued and paid when taken. Increases to 6% after 5 years.

steps.title: Gross Pay
steps.description: Start with annual salary / pay periods.

steps.title: Deduct CPP & EI
steps.description: Subtract pension and insurance contributions first (they generate tax credits).

steps.title: Deduct Income Tax
steps.description: Calculate Federal and Provincial tax based on taxable income brackets.

steps.title: Net Pay
steps.description: Result is the take-home amount.

items.title: Due Dates
items.text: Remittances are typically due by the 15th of the month following the payout.

items.title: Late Penalties
items.text: Late remittances incur a 3% to 10% penalty depending on the severity of the delay.

items.title: Electronic Filing
items.text: Use the CRA 'My Business Account' portal for the fastest and most reliable remittance reporting.

heroData.title: Register a Corporation
heroData.subtitle: Federal or Provincial
heroData.description: Choose between Canada Business Corporations Act (Federal) or Provincial Acts. Federal offers name protection nationwide.

steps.title: Name Search (Nuans)
steps.description: Perform Nuans search ($13.80) to ensure name availability. Federal names must be unique across Canada.

steps.title: Articles of Incorporation
steps.description: Draft Form 1. Define share classes (Common Class A, B, etc.) and restrictions on share transfers.

steps.title: File & Pay
steps.description: Submit via Online Filing Centre ($200 fee). Certificate of Incorporation issued immediately via email upon approval.

steps.title: Tax Registration
steps.description: CRA automatically assigns a Business Number (BN). You must manually register for GST/HST, Payroll, and Import/Export program accounts.

steps.title: Minute Book
steps.description: Set up digital or physical minute book with bylaws, director resolutions, and share certificates.

items.title: Residency Removed
items.text: Federal, Ontario, Alberta, and BC corporations NO LONGER require 25% Canadian resident directors. Foreigners can own 100%.

items.title: Trade Name vs Corp
items.text: Incorporating protects your name. A simple 'trade name' or 'sole proprietorship' does not provide liability protection.

items.title: Federal vs Provincial
items.text: Choose Federal for nationwide name protection. Choose Provincial if you only operate locally and want to avoid annual federal filings.

faqs.question: Do I need a physical address in Canada?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need a Registered Office Address (cannot be a PO Box). Many law firms or virtual office providers offer this service.

faqs.question: What is the minimum share capital?
faqs.answer: There is no minimum. You can incorporate with $1.00.

heroData.title: Canadian Recruiting
heroData.subtitle: Tech & Engineering Talent
heroData.description: Strong talent pools in Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal. Agencies assist with navigating diverse candidate expectations.

steps.title: Agency Briefing
steps.description: Define role requirements, budget, and 'must-haves' vs 'nice-to-haves'. Sign fee agreement.

steps.title: Candidate Shortlist
steps.description: Agency presents 3-5 vetted candidates. Verify if they have Canadian work authorization.

steps.title: Interviews
steps.description: Remote or in-person. Behavioural questions are standard. Technical tests common for dev roles.

steps.title: Offer & Background Check
steps.description: Extend offer clearly stating 'probationary period' (3 months standard). Run criminal/credit checks if relevant.

items.title: Tech Hubs
items.text: Waterloo/Toronto is the 'Silicon Valley of the North'. Vancouver has strong gaming/visual effects talent. Montreal is an AI research hub.

items.title: Replacement Guarantee
items.text: Standard agency contracts include a 90-day replacement guarantee. If the hire leaves within 3 months, they find a replacement for free.

items.title: Remote Salaries
items.text: US companies hiring remotely in Canada have driven up tech salaries significantly. Expect to pay near-US rates for top senior talent.

faqs.question: Can I ask about Canadian experience?
faqs.answer: Strictly speaking, requiring 'Canadian experience' can be discriminatory under human rights laws unless BFOR. Focus on verifyable skills.

faqs.question: What is the standard vacation offering?
faqs.answer: 2 weeks is legal minimum, but 3-4 weeks is the market standard for professional/white-collar roles.

heroData.title: HR Platforms
heroData.subtitle: Managing Canadian Workforce
heroData.description: Tools like Humi, Rise, and Collage designed for Canadian specific compliance (vacation accrual, tax forms).

items.title: Canadian Winners
items.text: Humi, Collage, and Rise People are built specifically for Canadian compliance (TD1s, provincial taxes). US tools like Rippling/Gusto are entering but check for full localization.

items.title: CRA Integration
items.text: Look for 'ROE Web' automation. The ability to submit Records of Employment directly to Service Canada saves hours of manual work.

items.title: Quebec Support
items.text: Not all HRIS platforms verify support for RL-1 slips (Quebec T4 equivalent) or CNESST returns. Verify if you have QC employees.

steps.title: Data Cleansing
steps.description: Ensure current employee data (SINs, addresses, banking info) is accurate before import.

steps.title: Payroll YTD Load
steps.description: Load Year-to-Date payroll values to ensure T4s at year-end are correct.

steps.title: Policy Configuration
steps.description: Set up time-off policies (vacation accrual rules vary by province) and benefits deduction logic.

steps.title: Parallel Run
steps.description: Run at least one pay cycle on both old and new systems to match net pay to the penny.

faqs.question: Can I use US software?
faqs.answer: Only if it has a dedicated Canadian edition. US tax logic (W2, 401k) does not work here (T4, RRSP).

faqs.question: Is data stored in Canada?
faqs.answer: Many Canadian organizations prefer or require domestic data residency (PIPEDA compliance). Humi/Collage typically host in Canada (AWS ca-central-1).

heroData.title: CPA Services
heroData.subtitle: Bookkeeping & Tax Filing
heroData.description: Maintain financial records and ensure GST/HST/QST compliance.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping
steps.description: Reconcile bank statements, categorize expenses (Xero/QBO), and track receivables.

steps.title: Sales Tax Remittance
steps.description: File GST/HST (and QST/PST) returns based on assigned frequency (Monthly/Quarterly/Annual).

steps.title: Year-End Adjustments
steps.description: Accountant prepares adjusting entries (depreciation, accruals) after fiscal year close.

steps.title: T2 Filing
steps.description: File T2 Corporate Income Tax Return within 6 months of year-end. Balance of tax due within 2 (or 3) months.

items.title: Installments
items.text: If you owe >$3,000 in tax (GST or Income) in a year, CRA will require quarterly installments the following year.

items.title: Meals & Entertainment
items.text: Only 50% of food/drink costs for business meetings are deductible.

items.title: Cloud Ecosystem
items.text: QuickBooks Online and Xero are standard. Use tools like Dext (Receipt Bank) to digitize receipts for audit proofing.

faqs.question: When is my corporate tax due?
faqs.answer: The return (T2) is due 6 months after fiscal year-end. Tax PAYMENTS are due 2 months (or 3 for CCPCs) after year-end.

faqs.question: Do I need an audit?
faqs.answer: Private companies generally do not require an audit unless requested by a lender or shareholders. A 'Notice to Reader' (Compilation) is standard.

steps.title: Workers' Compensation Registration
steps.description: Register with provincial boards (WSIB in ON, CNESST in QC, WorkSafeBC in BC) within 15-30 days of hiring first employee.

steps.title: Employer Health Tax (EHT)
steps.description: Set up accounts for provincial payroll taxes where applicable (BC, ON, MB, QC) if annual payroll exceeds exemption thresholds.

steps.title: Health & Safety Policy
steps.description: Post mandatory Health & Safety posters and draft a provincial-compliant Workplace Violence and Harassment policy.

items.title: Common Law Notice
items.text: Canada is very pro-employee. Termination notice is based on 'Bardal Factors' (age, tenure, role) and often vastly exceeds statutory ESA minimums (e.g. 1 month per year of service is common rule of thumb).

items.title: PIPEDA Privacy
items.text: Federal privacy law governs how you collect, use, and store personal data. You must appoint a Privacy Officer.

items.title: Termination Clauses
items.text: Have a lawyer draft your employment contract termination clauses. If valid, they can limit liability to ESA minimums. If invalid, Common Law applies.

faqs.question: Are non-competes enforceable?
faqs.answer: In Ontario, Non-Compete agreements are ILLEGAL for most employees (as of 2021). Non-solicitation clauses are preferred.

faqs.question: What is the 'Right to Disconnect'?
faqs.answer: Ontario law requires employers with 25+ staff to have a written policy on disconnecting from work (after hours emails, etc.).

items.title: SR&ED Credits
items.text: The Scientific Research & Experimental Development (SR&ED) program offers a 35% refundable tax credit for CCPCs on eligible R&D spend (up to $3M limit).

items.title: Associated Corporations
items.text: If you own multiple corporations, they must SHARE the $500,000 Small Business Deduction (SBD) limit. You cannot duplicate the low rate.

items.title: Dividends vs Salary
items.text: Paying yourself via dividends avoids CPP contributions but reduces RRSP room. Salary builds RRSP room and CPP but requires monthly source deductions.

steps.title: Determine Residency
steps.description: Ensure 'Mind and Management' stays in Canada to maintain CCPC status.

steps.title: Calculate Net Income
steps.description: Adjust GAAP accounting income to Taxable Income (Schedule 1 adjustments).

steps.title: File T2 Return
steps.description: Submit electronically via EFILE. Mandatory for corporations.

steps.title: Issue T5 Slips
steps.description: If dividends were declared, file T5 slips by Feb 28th of the following year.

faqs.question: What is a CCPC?
faqs.answer: Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation. It qualifies for the low small business tax rate and enhanced R&D credits.

faqs.question: Can I claim home office expenses?
faqs.answer: Corporations can reimburse employees (including owners) for reasonable home office expenses if a signed T2200 form is provided.

heroData.title: Legal Contracts
heroData.subtitle: Commercial & Employment
heroData.description: Common law applies everywhere except Quebec (Civil Code).

items.title: Governing Law
items.text: Ontario law is the most common choice for English contracts. Avoid Quebec law unless necessary (Civil Code is distinct from Common Law).

items.title: Moral Rights
items.text: Canadian IP Assignment must explicitly waive 'Moral Rights' (author's right to integrity of work). A standard US assignment might miss this.

items.title: Regulation 105
items.text: A 15% withholding tax applies to fees paid to non-residents for services rendered IN Canada. Waivers can be applied for.

steps.title: Scope & Deliverables
steps.description: Define Service Level Agreements (SLAs) clearly.

steps.title: Confidentiality & IP
steps.description: Ensure IP assignment includes 'present assignment of future rights' and Moral Rights waiver.

steps.title: Indemnification
steps.description: Standard caps on liability (e.g. 12 months fees) are common.

steps.title: Dispute Resolution
steps.description: Specify arbitration vs court. Toronto is a major arbitration hub.

items.title: Civil Law System
items.text: Quebec uses Civil Law (Napoleonic) rather than Common Law. Contracts MUST be in French to be valid for employees in Quebec (Bill 96).

items.title: Bilingual Contracts
items.text: While bilingual is possible, the French version prevails in Quebec courts unless the parties explicitly agree otherwise (with limitations).

items.title: Local Versioning
items.text: Always maintain a Quebec-specific template if you have employees in Montreal or Gatineau.

items.title: Wekerle Standard
items.text: Termination clauses are strictly scrutinized. If they violate statutory minimums even slightly, they are void, and Common Law applies.

items.title: Severability
items.text: Ensure your MSA has robust severability clauses to prevent the entire contract being voided by one invalid clause.

items.title: Just Cause
items.text: Just cause is extremely difficult to prove in Canada. Most terminations are 'without cause'.

heroData.title: Tech Ecosystem
heroData.subtitle: Innovative North
heroData.description: Canada is a global leader in AI (Montreal), FinTech (Toronto), and Quantum Computing (Waterloo).

items.title: SR&ED Program
items.text: The Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax incentive is the largest single source of federal government support for industrial R&D. CCPCs can earn a refundable investment tax credit of 35% on up to $3 million of qualified expenditures.

items.title: IRAP Grants
items.text: NRC IRAP provides financial support to qualified small and medium-sized enterprises in Canada to undertake technology innovation. Unlike SR&ED, this is often grant-based (non-repayable or conditionally repayable) and can cover salary costs.

items.title: Data Residency
items.text: Public sector clients (gov, health) often require data to reside physically in Canada. Ensure your cloud architecture (AWS ca-central-1, Azure Canada Central) complies.

steps.title: IP Assignment
steps.description: Ensure all developers sign strict IP assignment agreements waiving moral rights.

steps.title: Access Grants
steps.description: Apply for 'hiring grants' (e.g., wage subsidies for SWPP co-op students) BEFORE the employee starts.

steps.title: Choose Structure
steps.description: Decide between hiring EOR (fast) or establishing a sub (better for SR&ED).

items.title: Montreal AI Ecosystem
items.text: Home to Mila and world-class researchers like Yoshua Bengio. One of the highest concentrations of AI talent globally.

items.title: Vector Institute
items.text: Toronto's Vector Institute provides industry collaboration for AI startups and enterprises.

items.title: IP Protection
items.text: Ensure AI-generated code ownership is explicitly covered in developer contracts.

heroData.title: Digital Agencies
heroData.subtitle: Growth Partners
heroData.description: Full-service agencies must navigate strict anti-spam (CASL) and language laws (Bill 96).

steps.title: Define Scope & Budget
steps.description: Clearly define deliverables (e.g. SEO audit, rebrand). Canadian agencies typically charge $150-$200/hr blended rate.

steps.title: RFP / Pitch
steps.description: For projects >$50k, issue an RFP. Review 3 agencies. Ask for case studies in your specific vertical.

steps.title: Contract Review
steps.description: Ensure IP ownership transfer is explicit. Verify CASL compliance warranties are included in the MSA.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Grant access to analytics/ad accounts. Set clear KPIs (CAC, ROAS) for the first 90 days.

items.title: CASL (Anti-Spam)
items.text: Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation is one of the strictest in the world. You CANNOT send commercial electronic messages (CEMs) without express or implied consent. Penalties: up to $10M for corporations.

items.title: Bill 96 (Quebec)
items.text: All marketing materials, websites, and contracts directed at the Quebec market MUST be available in French. 'French First' rules apply to signage and commercial publications.

items.title: Ad Standards
items.text: Ad Standards Canada regulates truth in advertising. Influencer marketing requires clear disclosure ('#ad' or '#sponsored').

faqs.question: Does CASL apply to B2B emails?
faqs.answer: Yes. Unless you have a pre-existing business relationship or the recipient notably published their address without a disclaimer, cold emailing is risky.

faqs.question: Are email lists legal to buy?
faqs.answer: Generally, NO. You cannot rely on third-party consent. Buying a list and emailing them is a direct violation of CASL unless you can prove obtained consent.
